title: SUNDAY ROAST
synopsis: A widowed father invites his three estranged adult children home for a Sunday roast. Over one meal, thirty years of resentment, forgiveness, and the letter their mother left unopened all land on the table.

characters.name: Julia Merrick
characters.role: Eldest daughter — 41, corporate, drove up from Manchester

characters.name: Tom Merrick
characters.role: Middle son — 38, teacher, brought his partner

characters.name: Priya Ali
characters.role: Tom's partner — new to the family

key_props.name: Mother's Letter
key_props.description: A sealed envelope in her handwriting, addressed 'To be opened when we're all together.' Sits on the mantel in Scenes 1-8. Opened in Scene 9. Its contents are shown to no one but the audience.

key_props.name: Sunday Roast
key_props.description: Lamb, potatoes, greens. Comes out of the oven in Scene 6 whole; is at various states of eaten from Scene 7 onward. Continuity trap: it must age plausibly across the dinner sequence.

key_props.name: Sam's Ring
key_props.description: Sam's engagement ring — never mentioned aloud, only visible on their hand from Scene 3 onward. Frank notices it in Scene 7 but says nothing until Scene 10.

key_props.name: The Wine
key_props.description: A bottle Frank has been saving. Level in the glass and bottle must decrease consistently across scenes 6-11.

demo_scenario.description: The dressing-a-set demo: a re-shoot of Scene 8 accidentally uses a full wine bottle when Scene 7 already showed it half-drunk. CASCADE traces the impact: 4 scenes need matching bottle levels, and Priya's glass in Scene 9 must reflect what she poured in Scene 8. Continuity is what makes a small drama look expensive.

notes_for_agents: This is intentionally the OPPOSITE of THE LAST SIGNAL — one house, one meal, one afternoon, four days of shooting. If CONTINUUM handles Scene 42 of a 47-scene sci-fi thriller AND the wine-level continuity of a 12-scene chamber drama with the same agent set, that's genre-independence.
Skeptic should route through here often — chamber drama is where 'the director meant it that way' is a genuine and frequent counter-argument to a continuity finding.
FinalTake's wrap decisions here hinge on coverage ratios that are much tighter than TLS-001 (shorter scenes, fewer angles, less room to fix in post).
